text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. on Tuesday reported higher-than-expected, first-quarter earnings amid strength in the computer products, service and support segment.
For the quarter ended Jan. 31, 1997, Hewlett-Packard earned $912 million, or 87 cents a share, compared with $790 million, or 75 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
Industry analysts had predicted it would earn 75 cents a share, according to First Call Inc., which tracks analyst predictions.
Revenues for the quarter rose to $10.3 billion from $9.29 billion a year earlier., the Palo Alto, Calif.-based computer maker said.
However, Chairman Lewis Platt said the company expects an "extremely challenging" competitive market in coming months and will manage expenses and assets carefully.

The company said overall orders grew 9 percent, which "was a bit slower than we would have liked," Platt said. "But we consider 9 percent growth acceptable in light of the many factors that affected orders, including a tough comparison with last year and the impact of currency exchange rates."

Orders for the quarter were $11.0 billion, compared with $10.1 billion in last year's first quarter. Without the effects of currency exchange rates, the company's order growth would have been approximately 2 percentage points higher, Hewlett-Packard said.
Orders for HP LaserJet printers grew moderately during the quarter, with the recently introduced HP LaserJet 6P printer being very well received, the company said.
"Our ability to manage costs and expenses carefully was a key driver of our earnings growth," said Platt.
Hewlett-Packard stock was off 87.5 cents to close at $49.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
